comments: Fourth run in the leaky0125+2w+1 hardware-scheme series. Three prior runs (quant_freeze_iters 60000/76000/92000, all dropout_rate=0.1) all share the exact same deterministic epoch-126 peak (val dice 0.3468) since they're identical up to whichever freeze point is smallest, then diverge only in post-freeze stability: freeze=60000 eventually collapsed to trivial all-background by epoch 285; freeze=76000 and freeze=92000 both stayed stable through epoch 300 but plateaued at the same 0.3468 ceiling, never climbing further. So freeze timing controls collapse risk but not the ceiling -- 3/3 runs cap at ~0.35, well below the old w=w scheme's 0.3757. This run keeps the stable freeze=76000 point and instead drops dropout_rate 0.1 -> 0.0, testing whether the 2*w_stored+1 weight-multiply datapath's own structural noise (an unlearnable, per-position 'sum(x) over receptive field' term added to every conv, since w_eff's '+1' isn't scaled by anything trainable -- see kurals/models/quant.py) is already enough of an involuntary regularizer that the usual 0.1 dropout (tuned for the old, noise-free w=w scheme) is now redundant/over-regularizing on top of it, capping achievable dice below what's actually reachable. Not confirmed -- a plausible mechanism, not a proven one; if this doesn't move the ceiling either, the 2w+1 scheme's ~0.35 cap should be treated as load-bearing (see CLAUDE.md's SoC section) rather than something to keep chasing without a new hypothesis.
